title: Reversible changes
keyIdea: A reversible change can be undone: melting, freezing, dissolving and mixing make no new material.

kid: Melt ice and you get water. Freeze it and you get ice back. That change can go back, so it is reversible.
No new material is made. It is still water.
adult: Changes of state (melting, freezing, boiling, condensing), dissolving and mixing are reversible: the same material comes back. Burning, rusting and cooking make new materials, so they are irreversible.
A good test: can you get the starting materials back by a simple method such as cooling, heating, filtering or evaporating? If yes, it is reversible.

familyTip: Make ice lollies from juice, then melt one. Is it the same juice? Now toast bread: can you untoast it?

practice.hint: Think what happens when you cool it.
Can you get the paper back?

practice.prompt: {n} ice cubes melt, then all refreeze. How many ice cubes?
practice.explain: Melting is reversible, so all {n} ice cubes come back.

practice.prompt: You dissolve {n} g of salt and evaporate the water. How many grams of salt do you get back?
practice.hint: Dissolving is reversible, so nothing is lost.
practice.explain: All the salt is left behind: {n} g comes back.

pool.hint: It is still the same stuff afterwards.
